learningObjective: Explain when CUDA Graphs help LLM inference and what limitation they impose on batch composition.

canonicalClaims.claim: CUDA Graphs amortize per-kernel launch overhead by capturing a sequence of kernels once and replaying it many times; the trade-off is that shapes and memory layouts must match the captured version, requiring per-shape graphs.
conditions: Kernels have static shapes at capture time.
Pointers referenced by the graph remain valid across replays.
nonImplications: Does not fuse or reorder kernels.
Does not eliminate GPU-side compute time.

misconceptions.claim: CUDA Graphs fuse kernels into fewer hardware kernels.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They replay the same kernels; no fusion.

misconceptions.claim: CUDA Graphs help only compute-bound workloads.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They help when launch overhead is the bottleneck, which is common in memory-bound decode with many small kernels.

misconceptions.claim: CUDA Graphs are incompatible with continuous batching.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Frameworks capture graphs for a set of common batch sizes and fall back to eager for uncommon shapes.

implementationFacts: vLLM captures decode CUDA Graphs for common batch sizes (e.g., powers of two up to max batch).
For prefill, graphs are less useful because prefill kernels are larger and launch overhead is a smaller fraction.
performanceScenarios: LLM decode with 20-50 kernels per step benefits from graphs; large prefill matmuls do not.
